P.w: One of the world's great art museums — 300,000 works including Seurat's La Grande Jatte, Hopper's Nighthawks and Wood's American Gothic.

P.ad: 1400 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
P.w: The 1893-born natural history museum on the Museum Campus — home of SUE the T. rex and Máximo the titanosaur.
The 103rd-floor observation deck of the former Sears Tower, with The Ledge glass boxes 1,353 ft over Wacker Drive.

P.ad: Millennium Park, 201 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60602
P.w: Anish Kapoor's mirror-polished 'Bean' in Millennium Park — the requisite Chicago selfie, beside Gehry's Pritzker Pavilion and the Lurie Garden. Free.
P.k: public art sculpture icon park free

P.w: The 1916 pier stretching into Lake Michigan, with the 200-ft Centennial Wheel, the Chicago Children's Museum and boat departures.
Grant Park's 1927 Versailles-inspired fountain, one of the largest in the world, with summer light-and-water shows. Free.

P.ad: 1300 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
P.w: The first planetarium in the Western Hemisphere (1930), at the tip of Northerly Island's peninsula with a classic skyline view.
The 1869 limestone water tower that survived the Great Chicago Fire, now a free city art gallery on the Mag Mile.

P.ad: 5700 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60637
P.w: The largest science centre in the Western Hemisphere, in the 1893 World's Fair Palace of Fine Arts — U-505 submarine, coal mine, Pioneer Zephyr.
The Cubs' ivy-walled ballpark (1914), the second-oldest in the majors, with its hand-turned scoreboard and Wrigleyville rooftops.

P.ad: 300 N Central Park Ave, Chicago, IL 60624
P.w: Jens Jensen's 1908 'landscape art under glass' — one of the largest conservatories in the US, with free admission.
One of the country's oldest zoos (1868) and still free, with the Farm-in-the-Zoo and Nature Boardwalk.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1910 Prairie School masterpiece in Hyde Park, inscribed by UNESCO in The 20th-Century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright. Tours by the FLW Trust.
P.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

P.w: The 1897 former public library, now the nation's first free municipal cultural center — under the world's largest Tiffany glass dome (38 ft, ~30,000 pieces).
Burnham & Root's 1888 LaSalle Street landmark, whose skylit light court was remodelled by Frank Lloyd Wright in 1905 — the spiral oriel staircase is the money shot.
P.k: architecture building frank lloyd wright landmark

P.w: The 1921 French Baroque movie palace under the six-storey C-H-I-C-A-G-O marquee on State Street.

Hood & Howells' 1925 Gothic tower from the 'most beautiful building in the world' competition, its base studded with ~150 fragments of famous buildings (Westminster Abbey, the Great Wall, the Parthenon).
The tapering, X-braced former John Hancock Center (1969), with the 94th-floor 360 Chicago observation deck and TILT.
Bertrand Goldberg's 1963 'corncob' towers on the river — at opening the tallest residential and tallest concrete buildings in the world.
Frank Gehry's ribbon-steel bandshell in Millennium Park — free summer concerts (Grant Park Music Festival) and movies on the lawn.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1908 poured-concrete temple in Oak Park — part of UNESCO's 20th-Century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright inscription.

P.n: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio
P.w: Where Wright lived and worked 1889–1909 and developed the Prairie style; a National Historic Landmark, toured by the Frank Lloyd Wright Trust.
P.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

P.ad: 11141 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL 60628
P.w: George Pullman's 1880s company town — the clock-tower factory, Hotel Florence and rowhouses; site of the 1894 strike and the Pullman porters' story. NPS unit since 2015.
The lace-domed 1953 Baháʼí temple on the Wilmette lakefront — the oldest surviving Baháʼí House of Worship in the world, with formal gardens.
Pilsen's free museum of Mexican art — one of the largest Latinx cultural institutions in the US (10,000+ works); its Día de Muertos show is a city ritual.
Founded 1961 in Washington Park — the oldest independent African American museum in the country.
One of the largest contemporary art museums in the world, in Streeterville off the Mag Mile; Tuesday summer jazz on the terrace.
The city's history museum at the south end of Lincoln Park — Lincoln's deathbed, the Great Fire, and an exhibit on the Chicago hot dog.
Chicago's oldest and largest continuously running blues club (1968) — two stages, alternating sets until 4 a.m.
The South Loop blues club owned by Buddy Guy himself — live blues every night and his own January residency.
One of the city's best-known jazz rooms, two blocks off the Mag Mile, with nightly sets and jam sessions.
Uptown's 1907 former Capone-era speakeasy, one of the oldest continuously operating jazz clubs in the country; home of the Uptown Poetry Slam.
P.k: jazz club speakeasy cocktail bar music

P.w: Old Town's improv theatre (1959) that launched Belushi, Murray, Fey, Colbert and Carell.

P.ad: Washington Park community area, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
P.w: Olmsted & Vaux's 372-acre South Side park, home of Lorado Taft's 'Fountain of Time' and the DuSable museum.

P.ad: Evanston lakefront, IL (per NPS NHL record)
P.w: Château-style 1894 lakefront mansion of Nobel laureate and US Vice President Charles G. Dawes — a National Historic Landmark run by the Evanston History Center.

P.ad: Lower West Side (Pilsen), around 18th St, Chicago (per Wikipedia / City of Chicago landmark district)
P.w: National Register district of 1870s–1910s Bohemian worker cottages, storefronts and churches — now the heart of Mexican Pilsen and its murals along 16th and 18th Streets.

P.ad: 300 N Central Park Ave, Chicago, IL
P.w: The 1928 Spanish Baroque 'Gold Dome' fieldhouse, a gold-leafed Chicago Landmark towering over Garfield Park — under a $9M restoration.

P.n: Holy Cross Church (Back of the Yards)
P.w: National Register Lithuanian church (1915) whose twin towers rise over Back of the Yards, the old stockyards neighbourhood.

P.n: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary (Marquette Park)
P.w: Mid-century Lithuanian Catholic church facing Marquette Park, designed in Lithuanian folk style — the spiritual centre of Chicago's Lithuanian community.

P.ad: W 47th St a few blocks east of S Ashland Ave, Back of the Yards, Chicago
P.w: A 93,500 sq ft former meatpacking plant turned net-zero vertical farm and food-business incubator, home to Whiner Beer.
George Pullman's 1881 Queen Anne hotel at the heart of his company town — now restored within Pullman National Historical Park.

P.ad: 11211 S St Lawrence Ave, Chicago, IL
P.w: Pullman's 1882 serpentine-greenstone church, designed by Solon S. Beman as part of the model town.
The ensemble theatre founded in 1974 by Gary Sinise, Terry Kinney and Jeff Perry — Tony-winning home of Malkovich, Metcalf and 'August: Osage County'.

P.n: Old Town School of Folk Music
P.w: Folk-music school and concert hall (founded 1957) in a restored 1929 library building on Lincoln Square's main street.

P.ad: 2045 N Lincoln Park West (in Lincoln Park), Chicago, IL
P.w: The last tomb left from the old City Cemetery under Lincoln Park — Ira Couch's 1858 mausoleum, too heavy to move.
The garage site of Capone-era Chicago's most notorious hit (1929) — the building is gone; a fenced lawn marks the spot.

P.ad: Division St between Western Ave and California Ave, Chicago, IL 60622
P.w: Humboldt Park's Puerto Rican main street, bracketed by two 59-ft, 45-ton steel Puerto Rican flags arching over Division Street — a designated Chicago Landmark.

P.ad: Forest Ave, Oak Park, IL (per Wikipedia)
P.w: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1902 Prairie-style house on Forest Avenue — low roman-brick walls and a raised main floor, a National Historic Landmark.
P.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

P.n: Roberts Temple Church of God in Christ
P.w: Bronzeville church where Mamie Till-Mobley held her son Emmett Till's open-casket funeral in 1955 — part of the Emmett Till and Mamie Till-Mobley National Monument (2023).

P.ad: 4339 S Lake Park Ave, Chicago, IL
P.w: Kenwood two-flat where Muddy Waters lived and rehearsed (1954–74) — a Chicago Landmark being restored as the MOJO Muddy Waters museum.

P.ad: 2700 S Halsted St area (former Stearns Quarry), Bridgeport, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
P.w: A 1830s limestone quarry turned 27-acre park — a fishing pond in the pit, terraced wetlands and the city's best skyline hill.

P.ad: New City / Back of the Yards, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
P.w: Olmsted Brothers & Burnham 'neighbourhood park' (1905) ringed by a lagoon, with a Burnham-designed fieldhouse — a landmark of the South Parks reform movement.

P.ad: Back of the Yards, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
P.w: One of the first 1905 South Parks small parks, built to give stockyards families a fieldhouse, baths and playgrounds.

P.ad: South Fork of the South Branch, Chicago River (headwaters, per Wikipedia)
P.w: The stockyards' notorious waste channel — Upton Sinclair's 'Bubbly Creek' still burps methane from century-old sediment, now ringed by new trails.
Historic African American cemetery — resting place of Emmett Till, Dinah Washington and Willie Dixon.

P.n: Emmett Till and Mamie Till-Mobley House
P.ad: 6427 S St Lawrence Ave, Chicago, IL
P.w: The West Woodlawn two-flat Emmett Till left in 1955 — a Chicago Landmark (2021) being restored as a museum and community space.

P.n: R. W. Evans House (Frank Lloyd Wright)
P.w: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1908 hilltop Prairie house on Beverly's Longwood Drive ridge.
P.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

P.ad: 1600–1800 blocks of W 104th Pl (Griffin Place), Beverly, Chicago
P.w: A street of Prairie School houses (1909–14), seven by Walter Burley Griffin — later the designer of Canberra — a Chicago Landmark district.

P.ad: South Deering, east shore of Lake Calumet, Chicago
P.w: A former slag dump turned the Park District's largest natural site (~300 acres) — wetlands, birding and a bike park with pump tracks.
A 257-acre forest preserve inside city limits on Beverly's ridge — trails, a sledding hill and the Major Taylor Trail.

P.n: National A. Philip Randolph Pullman Porter Museum
P.w: Museum of the Pullman porters and the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters — the birthplace of Black labor history, within Pullman National Historical Park.

P.ad: Ukrainian Village, Chicago, IL 60622 (street number pending re-verify)
P.w: 1915 Neo-Byzantine cathedral modelled on Kyiv's St. Sophia — its thirteen copper domes crown Ukrainian Village; interior mosaics are among Chicago's finest.

P.ad: Logan Blvd, Kedzie Blvd & Palmer Sq around Logan Square, Chicago, IL 60647
P.w: The Northwest Side's grandest stretch of Chicago's boulevard system — graystone 'boulevard of the millionaires' mansions around Logan and Palmer squares (NRHP + Chicago Landmark district).

P.n: National Museum of Puerto Rican Arts and Culture
P.ad: Humboldt Park (1895 park stables), Chicago, IL 60622
P.w: The only US national museum devoted to Puerto Rican art, in Humboldt Park's 1895 stables — the park's oldest building.

P.ad: Milwaukee / North / Damen six-way intersection, Wicker Park, Chicago
P.w: The triangular 1929 Art Deco Northwest Tower — first skyscraper of its size outside downtown — at the six-way Milwaukee/North/Damen crossing, now a hotel with skyline rooftop bars.
Mother church of Chicago Polonia (1867–81, Patrick Keely) — by 1897 the largest parish in the US; a 'Polish Cathedral' landmark in Noble Square.

P.ad: Pierce Ave & Hoyne Ave around Wicker Park, Chicago, IL 60622
P.w: Victorian mansions of 'Beer Baron Row' (Hoyne) and Pierce Ave lining the 1870 park — one of the city's best post-Fire residential streetscapes (Chicago Landmark district).

P.ad: Alta Vista Terrace, Lakeview (Wrigleyville), Chicago, IL 60613
P.w: 'Street of Forty Doors' — a single block of London-style rowhouses (1900–04) mirrored end to end; Chicago's first designated historic district (1971), steps from Wrigley Field.

P.ad: W Argyle St, Uptown, Chicago, IL 60640
P.w: Where Charlie Chaplin made 'His New Job' and Gloria Swanson started out — the 1907 silent-film studio's terracotta-trimmed home, a Chicago Landmark (now St. Augustine College).
Brewer Francis Dewes's 1896 Lincoln Park mansion — exuberant German Baroque, with caryatids holding up the balcony; a Chicago Landmark beside his brother's matching house.
Freethinkers' cemetery founded 1877 by Czech immigrants — Bohemian-art monuments, Mayor Anton Cermak's grave and the Eastland-disaster victims; CAC-toured.
Olmsted & Vaux's 1869 curving-street suburb along the Des Plaines River — one of America's first planned communities, a National Historic Landmark (expanded 2023).
Wright's own 'most successful of my houses' (1906–09) — a long, low U-shaped Prairie complex set into Olmsted's Riverside; National Historic Landmark (private, exterior view).

P.n: Ward W. Willits House (Frank Lloyd Wright)
P.w: Widely considered Wright's first mature Prairie-style house (1901–02), on Highland Park's Sheridan Road — a National Historic Landmark (private, exterior view).

P.ad: 1200 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
P.w: 1930 Beaux-Arts aquarium on Museum Campus — 32,000 animals, beluga whales and Pacific white-sided dolphins in the lake-view Abbott Oceanarium.

P.ad: N Michigan Ave between Randolph St and Monroe St, Chicago, IL 60602
P.w: The 24.5-acre front lawn of Chicago (2004) — Cloud Gate, Crown Fountain, Gehry's Pritzker Pavilion and the hidden Lurie Garden, with free summer concerts.

P.ad: E Erie St, River North, Chicago (Nickerson Mansion)
P.w: The 1883 Nickerson 'Marble Palace' — marble floors, grand staircases and Gilded Age decorative arts, a block off Michigan Avenue.

P.ad: S Wentworth Ave, Chinatown, Chicago, IL 60616
P.w: The 1928 On Leong Merchants Association building — pagoda towers, green tile roofs and terracotta, Chinatown's signature landmark (Chicago Landmark 1993).

P.ad: S Wabash Ave, Bronzeville (Near South Side), Chicago
P.w: Home of Chicago's oldest Black congregation (1844), an Underground Railroad station; its 1892 sanctuary still stands at Bronzeville's northern edge (Chicago Landmark).
Birthplace of gospel music — Thomas A. Dorsey's 1931 choir here launched Mahalia Jackson and a new American sound (Chicago Landmark 2011).

P.n: Site of the Great Chicago Fire (Pillar of Fire)
P.w: Where the 1871 fire began in the O'Leary barn — now, fittingly, the CFD's Quinn Fire Academy, with Egon Weiner's bronze 'Pillar of Fire' and a plaque marking the spot (Chicago Landmark).

P.ad: Lakefront from North Ave to Ardmore Ave, Chicago (Chicago Park District)
P.w: Chicago's largest park (1868) — seven miles of lakefront with the free zoo, conservatory, North Pond, Caldwell Lily Pool, beaches and the Lakefront Trail.

P.ad: N Clark St around Foster & Balmoral Aves, Andersonville, Chicago
P.w: The old Swedish village on Clark Street — indie shops, Swedish bakeries and the flag-painted water tower; Time Out once voted it the coolest neighbourhood in the US (NRHP district).

P.ad: N Sheridan Rd at the north end of Lake Shore Drive, Edgewater, Chicago
P.w: The pink 1928 tower at the end of Lake Shore Drive — the surviving sister of the vanished Edgewater Beach Hotel resort (NRHP).

P.ad: 900–1100 blocks of W Bryn Mawr Ave (Sheridan Rd to Broadway), Edgewater, Chicago
P.w: Three blocks of 1897–1928 apartment hotels and terracotta façades once home to Chicago's elite — Bryn Mawr & Belle Shore hotels; made a Chicago Landmark district in Sept 2026.
An 1886 limestone 'Irish castle' on the Beverly ridge, built by developer Robert Givins for his bride — home of Beverly Unitarian Church since 1941.
181-acre East Side lakefront park with a sandy beach, a 1924 Classical Revival fieldhouse (Chicago Landmark) and a model-train exhibit; views to the Indiana steel shore.
Chicago's oldest public building (1856) and a Great Fire survivor — Celtic-revival windows and Book of Kells-inspired stencils in the West Loop.

P.ad: S Dearborn St at W Adams St, the Loop, Chicago
P.w: Holabird & Roche's 1895 Chicago School landmark — Tiffany mosaics of Père Marquette's voyage and Edward Kemeys bronzes in the lobby.

P.ad: N Michigan Ave, the Loop, Chicago (Pendry Chicago hotel)
P.w: The Burnham brothers' 1929 black-granite and gold-leaf Art Deco tower — said to be modelled on a champagne bottle — now the Pendry hotel with a rooftop bar.
Chicago's oldest house (1836), the Greek Revival home of Henry & Caroline Clarke, now a city-run museum in the Prairie Avenue district.
The city's architecture HQ on the river — supersized skyscraper models, the lit-up downtown model, and the departure dock for its famous 90-minute First Lady river cruise.

P.ad: S Michigan Ave, Prairie Avenue district, Chicago
P.w: Gothic Revival church re-done inside in Arts & Crafts style by Howard Van Doren Shaw after a 1900 fire — 21 stained-glass windows, nine by Tiffany (NHL).

P.ad: W Washington St, the Loop, Chicago
P.w: The 1924 First United Methodist 'Chicago Temple' — the world's tallest church building, with a tiny Sky Chapel in its spire 400 ft above the Loop.

P.ad: Irving Park — blocks around Avers & Hamlin Aves north of Addison St, Chicago
P.w: Seven boulevard blocks of 126 Prairie & Craftsman bungalows (1907–25) with double lots and deep setbacks — a hidden NRHP + Chicago Landmark district.
Rapp & Rapp's 1930 Gateway movie palace, restored as the Polish-American Copernicus cultural centre — concerts and dance most nights; next door to the Taste of Polonia festival.
America's leading museum of outsider and self-taught art — home of the recreated Henry Darger Room; reopened in 2025 after a major expansion.
Chicago Landmark district of worker cottages and two-flats around the onion-domed churches — the heart of the city's Ukrainian community (CAC walking tour).

P.n: Frank Lloyd Wright Historic District (Oak Park)
P.w: The world's largest concentration of Wright buildings — two dozen Prairie houses within walking distance of his Home & Studio; FLW Trust guided walks April–November.
P.k: frank lloyd wright architecture historic district

P.w: Northwestern's free art museum on the lakefill campus — prints, photography, film and ambitious exhibitions.
1929 glasshouse with 20,000 plants in Mediterranean, tropical and desert rooms — a free hidden gem south of downtown Oak Park.

P.ad: W Jackson Blvd between Laflin St and Ashland Ave, Near West Side, Chicago
P.w: A block of 1880s Victorian rowhouses and mansions that survived the West Side's decline — a Chicago Landmark district and NRHP listing.
1929 town hall at the heart of Austin — now a Chicago Park District cultural centre and fieldhouse with a historic auditorium.

P.ad: W Argyle St between Broadway and Sheridan Rd, Uptown, Chicago
P.w: Chicago's 'Little Saigon' — a few blocks of pho houses, bakeries and Asian markets around the Argyle 'L' stop (NRHP historic district; Asia on Argyle night market).

The 1890s market square at the centre of George Pullman's company town — once 16 market stalls and a meeting hall, ringed by colonnaded apartments still lived in today; now a public-art site in the national park.

P.ad: Division St / Milwaukee Ave / Ashland Ave, Wicker Park–Noble Square, Chicago
P.w: The plaza at the heart of old 'Polish Downtown', where nearly every major Polish-American organisation once had its headquarters — summer 'Tuesdays at the Triangle' events.
385 acres on nine islands in the Cook County Forest Preserves at Glencoe — 24 gardens, prairies and greenhouses; the winter Orchid Show.
The 216-acre Chicago Zoological Park in Brookfield — polar bears, the Seven Seas dolphins, Tropic World.
The 2.7-mile elevated rail-trail through Logan Square, Humboldt Park, Wicker Park and Bucktown. Free.

P.ad: 6401 S Stony Island Ave (Wooded Island, Jackson Park), Chicago, IL 60637
P.w: The Japanese garden on Jackson Park's Wooded Island, rooted in Japan's 1893 World's Fair pavilion; 160 cherry trees in spring. Free.
Victorian garden cemetery (1860) of Chicago's builders — Burnham, Sullivan, Mies, Marshall Field, Roger Ebert — with Lorado Taft's 'Eternal Silence'.
The Bears' colonnaded 1924 lakefront stadium (with its 2003 'spaceship' bowl), also home of the Chicago Fire.

P.n: Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures Museum
P.w: The University of Chicago's free museum of the ancient Near East (ex-Oriental Institute) — the 40-ton Khorsabad lamassu, Egypt, Persia, Mesopotamia.
The University of Chicago's soaring Gothic chapel, with a 72-bell carillon among the largest instruments ever built.

P.ad: 5491 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60615
P.w: Alfred Caldwell's limestone-stepped peninsula with a castle-like field house — a downtown-skyline view, swimming off the rocks and fire pits. Free.

P.ad: 7059 S South Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60649
P.w: The 1906 South Shore Country Club, now a Park District cultural center with a beach, nature sanctuary and golf — the Obamas held their wedding reception here.
H. H. Richardson's 1887 Romanesque fortress-house on Prairie Avenue, a museum of the Gilded Age.

P.ad: 50 E Ida B. Wells Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
P.w: Adler & Sullivan's 1889 Auditorium Building — a National Historic Landmark with a gold-leafed arched hall and famous acoustics.
Burnham & Root's 1891 load-bearing brick skyscraper — 'the first modern building' — with Holabird & Roche's steel-frame 1893 addition.
The 1925 Beaux-Arts station whose Great Hall rises under a 219-ft barrel-vaulted skylight — the Untouchables staircase.
The 1890s Victorian glasshouse in Lincoln Park — palms, ferns and orchids, free and open year-round.
15 miles of Lake Michigan beaches and towering dunes an hour from the Loop by the South Shore Line — Mount Baldy, the West Beach dune trails.
Sandstone canyons and seasonal waterfalls on the Illinois River, 90 minutes south-west of Chicago — Illinois's most-visited state park.
The two surviving buildings of Jane Addams's 1889 settlement house on the UIC campus — the birthplace of American social work. Free (suggested donation).
North America's oldest outdoor music festival — the Chicago Symphony's summer home; picnic on the lawn.
1,700 acres of trees in Lisle with 16 miles of trails and a children's garden; Illumination in winter.

P.ad: 700 N Art Museum Dr, Milwaukee, WI 53202
P.w: Calatrava's lakefront Quadracci Pavilion whose Burke Brise Soleil 'wings' open and close daily — 90 minutes north of Chicago.
The only Harley-Davidson Museum in the world — 450+ motorcycles on a 20-acre Menomonee Valley campus.
Louis Sullivan's only intact house of worship (1903), a Russian-village church in Ukrainian Village, part-funded by Tsar Nicholas II.

P.ad: 3100 W Logan Blvd (Logan Square), Chicago, IL 60647
P.w: The eagle-topped column at the heart of Logan Square (1918), by Henry Bacon of the Lincoln Memorial — the hub of the boulevard system.
One of the oldest and largest ethnic museums in the US (1935), in the old Polish Downtown.
Rapp & Rapp's 1925 'acre of seats in a magic city' — the largest movie palace ever built in Chicago, shuttered since 1981 and awaiting restoration (exterior only).
The 1926 Spanish-palace dance hall with a twinkling-star ceiling, now a rock venue.
The 1929 Southport movie palace with a starry-sky ceiling and a live organist between shows — Chicago's leading independent cinema.
The 1914 Lincoln Avenue movie house outside which John Dillinger was shot by the FBI in 1934; now Victory Gardens' stage.

P.ad: Washington Park, 5900 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL 60637
P.w: Lorado Taft's 1922 concrete procession of 100 figures passing before Father Time, at the west end of the Midway. Free.

P.ad: 6760 S Stony Island Ave, Chicago, IL 60649
P.w: Theaster Gates's restored 1923 bank — the Johnson Publishing library, Frankie Knuckles' records, galleries and free events.
P.k: gallery arts library house music free

P.w: Mies van der Rohe's 1956 glass-and-steel architecture school at IIT — widely held to be his finest work; a National Historic Landmark.

P.ad: 3500 S Dr Martin Luther King Jr Dr, Chicago, IL 60653
P.w: Bronzeville's 1928 memorial to the Black 8th Illinois regiment (370th Infantry) of WWI, won by a Chicago Defender campaign.
The 1879 Burnham & Root limestone gate — all that remains of the 475-acre Union Stock Yards that made Chicago 'hog butcher for the world'. A National Historic Landmark; free.
Where Martin Luther King Jr. marched for open housing in 1966 (and was struck by a rock); the Living Memorial's three pillars at Marquette Rd & Kedzie tell the Fair Housing story. Free.
The only museum in North America devoted to Lithuanian history and culture — in the city with the most Lithuanians outside Lithuania.

P.ad: Millennium Park, 201 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60602
P.w: Jaume Plensa's twin 50-ft glass-block towers in Millennium Park, projecting faces of Chicagoans who spout water into the splash pool. Free.
P.k: fountain public art park free family

P.ad: Daley Plaza, 50 W Washington St, Chicago, IL 60602
P.w: Picasso's untitled 50-ft Cor-ten steel sculpture (1967) in Daley Plaza — baboon, woman or dog, he never said. Free.

P.ad: Federal Plaza, 50 W Adams St, Chicago, IL 60603
P.w: Alexander Calder's 53-ft red stabile (1974) set against Mies van der Rohe's black Federal Center. Free.

P.ad: Chase Tower Plaza, 10 S Dearborn St, Chicago, IL 60603
P.w: Marc Chagall's 70-ft mosaic box (1974) of six Chicago scenes in 250 colours. Free.
20 acres east of Millennium Park — the climbing walls, the winter skating ribbon, mini golf and a giant playground. Free.

P.ad: Chicago River (main branch), Lake St to Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60601
P.w: The 1.25-mile path along the river's main branch — wine bars, kayak rentals and the city's best architecture at water level. Free.
Independent research library (1887) facing Washington Square — free exhibitions from 1.6 million books and 600,000 maps.
The world's largest public library building at opening (1991), with owl-topped acroterions and a 9th-floor winter garden. Free.
Chinatown's riverside park on an old rail yard — pagoda pavilion, kayak launch and the water-taxi stop. Free.
Small Chinatown museum on the Chinese journey to the Midwest, in the old Quong Yick warehouse.
Pilsen's 1892 hall modelled on the Prague opera house, now one of the city's favourite music venues (with Dusek's downstairs).
The Sunday open-air flea market descended from the 1880s Maxwell Street bazaar — tools, tires, produce and some of the city's best street tacos.
The Chicago Academy of Sciences' museum in Lincoln Park, built around the 2,700-sq-ft Judy Istock Butterfly Haven.

P.ad: Montrose Harbor (W Montrose Ave & Lake Shore Dr), Chicago, IL 60640
P.w: 15 lakefront acres where 300+ migratory species stop at 'the Magic Hedge'. Free.
Col. Robert McCormick's 500-acre Wheaton estate — gardens, his mansion, and the First Division tank museum.

P.n: Illinois Holocaust Museum and Education Center
P.w: Stanley Tigerman's Skokie museum founded by survivors, with its pioneering interactive survivor-hologram theatre.

P.ad: 339 N Oak Park Ave, Oak Park, IL 60302
P.w: The Queen Anne house where Hemingway was born in 1899, restored as a museum.
Evanston's 1873 lighthouse on the lake bluff, a National Historic Landmark; summer weekend tours.

P.ad: Forest Home Cemetery, 863 S Des Plaines Ave, Forest Park, IL 60130
P.w: The 1893 monument over the graves of the executed Haymarket anarchists — a pilgrimage site for May Day; surrounded by 'Radical Row'. National Historic Landmark.

P.ad: 373 W Geneva St, Williams Bay, WI 53191
P.w: The 1897 'birthplace of modern astrophysics' on Geneva Lake — home of the world's largest refracting telescope; tours.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1939 'dendriform'-columned Great Workroom and Research Tower in Racine — free tours by reservation.

P.ad: 1600 N Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60614
P.w: Chicago's busiest beach, by Lincoln Park — the ocean-liner beach house, volleyball, paddleboards and the classic skyline-across-the-sand view. Free.

P.ad: 1000 N Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60611
P.w: The Gold Coast beach at the top of the Mag Mile, tucked under the skyline. Free.

P.ad: 1200 S Linn White Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
P.w: Small crescent beach on Northerly Island behind the Adler, with panoramic lake views. Free.

P.ad: 1521 S Linn White Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
P.w: The man-made peninsula (the old Meigs Field) re-wilded with prairie paths, fishing spots and skyline views. Free.

Austin's soul-food cafeteria (1997) of Mississippi-born MacArthur Alexander — a West Side institution whose regulars included Barack Obama.
University Village corner stand (since 1929) — the Infatuation calls its jus the best in Chicago; cash-only ice counter next door.
Pilsen's Green-Restaurant-certified bar and cultural space — solar panels, salvaged fittings, a bar made from a bowling lane.

F.ad: 6257 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL 60637
F.w: Chicago's oldest restaurant — a Woodlawn lunch counter opened in 1892 for World's Fair builders; Muhammad Ali ate here between workouts. Moved across 63rd to Woodlawn Station in 2019.
Bridgeport's community bar run by the Marszewski family (Maria, from Busan) — with Kimski, the Korean-Polish kitchen added in 2016.
Casual, affordable Pilsen BYOB from chef Alfonso Sotelo (ex-Bayless) — Michelin-listed regional Mexican cooking.
Hyde Park's bar of record (1948) — Saul Bellow's 'local haunt', where students, professors and neighbours have always mixed.
James Beard winner Erick Williams' Louisiana tavern (2022) a block from his Virtue — live New Orleans jazz on first Wednesdays.

F.ad: S Halsted St at the Ramova Theatre, Bridgeport, Chicago
F.w: Bridgeport's 1929 Spanish-courtyard movie palace reborn in 2024 as a concert hall, with its old diner (famous for chili, closed 2012) and a brewery taproom beside it.
Chatham's vegan soul-food pioneer since 1982 (as Original Soul Vegetarian), renamed and renovated for its 40th year.

F.ad: E 47th St at S King Dr, Bronzeville, Chicago
F.w: Chef Cliff Rome's Bronzeville breakfast café — Southern brunch on 47th Street, with a visit from Barack Obama (WGN).
Chinatown's Hong Kong-style café for the late-night crowd — open till 4am most nights, 24 hours on weekends.
Chinatown's first speakeasy, a moody Blade Runner-esque lounge hidden behind Moon Palace Express — the family's restaurant still serves its soup dumplings up front.
Milwaukee-area custard stand since 1950 — one of the city's 'big three' with Gilles and Leon's; the Greenfield store is the original HQ.
Pilsen birrieria with a half-dozen-item menu — Time Out: 'one visit to this one before you stop caring about the rest.'
One of Pilsen's first coffeehouse-galleries (1994), opened by Eleazar Delgado in an old barber shop at 18th & Bishop — a neighbourhood living room for artists.

F.ad: Thalia Hall, S Allport St at 18th St, Pilsen, Chicago
F.w: CLOSED 31 Dec 2023: the Thalia Hall gastropub that won a Michelin star (2016) and helped revive Pilsen's 1892 hall; Thalia Hall's music room carries on.
Where Ike Sewell's 1943 pizzeria is credited with launching Chicago deep dish — the original still stands at Ohio & Wabash.
River North steakhouse (1987) named for the Cubs broadcaster, in a building once home to Capone enforcer Frank Nitti.
Rush Street power steakhouse since 1989 — consistently among the top-grossing independent restaurants in the US.
One of America's oldest continuously operating lunch-car diners (1926), hauled to Kenosha by six horses — on the National Register.
Milwaukee's neon-lit custard stand since the 1940s — said to have inspired Arnold's on Happy Days.

F.ad: 4629 N Port Washington Rd, Glendale, WI 53212
F.w: Glendale diner (1936) thought to have created the Wisconsin butter burger.

F.ad: N Clark St just north of Foster Ave, Andersonville, Chicago
F.w: The 'Anchor of Andersonville' since 1934 — founded by Swedish immigrant Simon Lundberg over his Prohibition-era No Name Club speakeasy.
Puerto Rican-owned bakery-café on Paseo Boricua a block from Humboldt Park — some of the city's best Puerto Rican coffee and pastries.
Paul Kahan's honky-tonk taco and whiskey bar at the Damen-Milwaukee crossroads of Wicker Park, with its packed summer patio.
The big Balmoral brewery and taproom (2017) of Half Acre, a staple of Chicago craft brewing since 2006.
Uptown's late-night honky-tonk — one of Chicago's last straight-up country bars, closed in 2016 and revived in 2018.
Lakeview dive at Clark & Belmont since the 1950s — Irish whiskey selection, a dark lore, and a stop on Anthony Bourdain's The Layover.
Six-table Edgewater counter where masa is patted and griddled to order — called the best huaraches in Chicago. Cash only.
Cash-only North Center taqueria — 'some of the freshest tacos in town' (Time Out); the Infatuation rates its carne asada 8.1.
Paul Kahan's 2008 Fulton Market beer hall of pork, oysters and beer — the restaurant that helped turn the meatpacking district into a dining destination.
Chicago's oldest Italian restaurant (1927), opened by Lucca-born Alfredo Capitanini and run by the fourth generation — a pre-opera Loop institution.
James Beard-winning chef Sarah Grueneberg's West Loop pasta house (2015), with sheets rolled and hung daily in view of the counter.
Beverly's neon-trimmed 1960 drive-in, revived in 2014 with its classic décor and menu intact — featured on Chicago's Best.
The 'Eat Sleep Whisky' gastropub-inn that put Logan Square on the dining map (Condé Nast Traveler); Michelin-listed in 2024.
Yelitza Rivera's Logan Square corner (2016) with the widest jibarito menu in town — lines out the door, now with a sit-down room next door.
Ravenswood's Neapolitan pizzeria with a quiet side-street patio — No. 14 in 50 Top Pizza USA 2023 and on its world top-100.
Loop pub since 1935 under the Wabash 'L' — signed photos from Sinatra to Monroe and one of the Loop's few late-night kitchens.

F.ad: Randolph St at Peoria St, West Loop, Chicago
F.w: Italian grocer since 1937, now in its fourth generation — its walk-up sub counter turns out some of the best sandwiches in the city.

F.ad: N Michigan Ave between Lake & Randolph (Millennium Park Plaza), Chicago
F.w: Chicago's popcorn icon since 1949 — the caramel-cheddar mix invented by customers in the 1970s; the Michigan Avenue shop's queue is a tourist-board photo.
Edgewater's Ethiopian dining room — the oldest Ethiopian restaurant in Chicago, nearly three decades on Broadway.
Small Buena Park Italian spot that invited TikTok critic Keith Lee (16M followers) — his visit produced a documented 'Keith Lee effect' surge (Fox32).
Lincoln Park's retro-pastel bakery — the city's go-to for old-fashioned buttercream cupcakes and bars.
Wrigleyville's best-known Cubs bar — a 1930s hot-dog stand (Ernie's, then Ray's Bleachers) facing the bleacher entrance at Sheffield & Waveland.

F.ad: Southport Ave at Henderson St, Lakeview, Chicago
F.w: CLOSED 2020 after 98 years: the last Chicago bowling alley with hand-set pins, in a former Schlitz tavern and Prohibition speakeasy; contents auctioned 2021.
Derrick Tung's Logan Square outpost of the Brooklyn pizzeria — his Detroit-style square won the 2018 U.S. Pizza Cup; a fixture of Time Out's essential-pizza list.
Wicker Park brewpub (2001) in an old bowstring-truss garage — 29 GABF/World Beer Cup medals, Chicago's most-awarded brewpub.
Humboldt Park's retro soda fountain and bakery — everything made in-house, with a salvaged 1920s Milwaukee marble counter.

F.ad: Milwaukee Ave at Gale St (SW corner), Jefferson Park, Chicago
F.w: Jefferson Park's oldest tavern-ribhouse (1963), by the Blue Line terminal — closed abruptly, then officially reopened (WGN).
Avondale Irish pub (1999) named for Chicago's Irish-music-collecting police chief Francis O'Neill — the only Chicago pick in a national top-50 Irish bars list.

F.ad: Old World Third Street, downtown Milwaukee, WI
F.w: Milwaukee's German restaurant since 1902 — a tavern turned Prohibition-era kitchen, still family-run on Old World Third Street.

F.ad: W St. Paul Ave, Milwaukee, WI
F.w: Milwaukee pub famous for its absurdly garnished bloody marys (a whole fried chicken on top) and some of the city's most popular burgers.
Milwaukee's first and Wisconsin's oldest frozen-custard stand (1938), built by Paul Gilles after he saw the lines at Chicago's 1933 World's Fair.
Family-run Loop pub since 1969 in a reputed Capone-era speakeasy — a less-crowded deep-dish alternative a block from Miller's Pub.

F.ad: 13th floor, Chicago Athletic Association hotel, S Michigan Ave, Chicago
F.w: The rooftop bar-restaurant of the 1893 Chicago Athletic Association — named Chicago's No. 1 rooftop restaurant by Time Out (2025), with a sweeping view of Millennium Park.

F.ad: 21st–22nd floors, LondonHouse hotel, Michigan Ave at Wacker Dr, Chicago
F.w: Indoor-outdoor rooftop bar on the 21st–22nd floors of the LondonHouse — one of the best vantage points on the Chicago River's architecture.

F.ad: W Devon Ave, West Ridge, Chicago
F.w: Devon Avenue's Pakistani standard-bearer since 1996 — Time Out says its namesake nihari will make you consider moving to Devon.
Argyle's Little Saigon anchor by the Red Line — the city's go-to pho house with a phone-book-length Vietnamese menu.
Mexican seafood house tucked into Thalia Hall from the Obelix / Taqueria Chingón team — whole fish from a wood-burning oven with tortillas and salsas.
Chef Thai Dang's 'unapologetically authentic' Vietnamese dining room in Pilsen — a James Beard-semifinalist kitchen and neighbourhood mainstay.
Pilsen's beloved ~50-year-old panadería — trays of conchas, cookies and fruit empanadas; its Three Kings roscas made the Sun-Times in 2026.
Latina-owned open-kitchen Mexican spot — seasonal mole and chile-laced beef soup, spice-adjustable margaritas, a strong Sunday brunch.

F.ad: W Taylor St, Little Italy, Chicago
F.w: Fourth-generation Taylor Street institution that grew from a 1909 bakery — still turning out thick, square bakery-style slices and hearty Italian-American plates.
French bistro hidden off the Taylor Street bustle — a locals' and critics' favourite with the neighbourhood's best patio and a deep wine list.
Evanston's taco-and-margarita stalwart — a dozen tacos, three to an order, with family-style beans and rice.
Small carry-out that grew out of the Evanston farmers' market — Latin American burritos, gorditas and empanadas with smart vegetarian fillings.

F.ad: 4248 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL 60653
F.w: Chef Kristen Harper's Creole-leaning Bronzeville soul-food counter — some of Chicago's best wings and fried chicken; Keith Lee's only 10/10 on his 2023 Chicago tour.

F.ad: S Cottage Grove Ave at E 44th St, Bronzeville, Chicago, IL 60653
F.w: Black-owned wine bar-restaurant from the Silver Room's owner — art-hung room, DJs and live music, a list that champions minority-owned producers.
The 'Med' — UChicago's hangout since 1963, booths carved with students' poetry and political rants; a breakfast-to-late menu.
Chinatown's dumpling specialist, risen from a Richland Center basement stand — ~40 fillings in three cooking styles, more varieties than anywhere in Chicago.
Chinatown's soup-dumpling specialist — xiaolongbao made fresh daily in full view of the dining room.

F.ad: 5200 S Archer Ave, Unit 8, Chicago, IL 60632
F.w: Family-run Archer Heights counter where scratch masa is the star — tlacoyos, picaditas, sopes and giant quesadillas (Infatuation 9.4).
Little Village taqueria that grew from Adan Lucido's home pop-up — al pastor carved to order off the spit with pineapple and salsa.
Beverly's Texas-style smokehouse — on the New York Times' 2025 list of the 50 best US restaurants and Jean Banchet Best Counter Service 2026.
James Beard-finalist baker Maya-Camille Broussard's social-mission pie shop in a former dentist's office on 87th Street.
Beverly's brewpub — a South Side destination for its beer, wood-fired pizza and 1,900 sq ft rooftop beer garden (new owners since May 2024).
Roseland steakhouse since 1969, Black-owned since 2018 — reopened in 2022 after the 2020 fire and looting.
McKinley Park warehouse taproom from the Maria's/Kimski family — wraparound bar, brewhouse views, arcade, karaoke and comedy nights.
Tiny McKinley Park family kitchen for Durango street food — svelte griddle-charred burritos and stuffed gorditas.
Devon Avenue's beloved cheap-eats institution — rich Indian/Pakistani plates at rock-bottom prices, open late.
Hema Potla's homestyle Indian kitchen on Devon — a Check, Please! and Reader favourite for decades.
All-vegetarian Devon Avenue standby spanning North and South India — dosas, chaat, curries and thalis.
Chef John Manion's smokehouse bolted onto historic FitzGerald's roadhouse — barbecue with live music every night.
The Westmont noodle legend's Oak Park outpost — springy hand-pulled noodles in ginger-chili broth and handmade dumplings.
Brewpub in the 1920 First National Bank of Oak Park — original dentil mouldings, award-winning pilsner and stouts.
Reservation-only soul-food fusion dining room on the ground floor of the North Lawndale building where Dr. King lived in 1966.
Chef Bridgette Flagg's soul-food restaurant — North Lawndale's first full-service sit-down restaurant in 50 years.
Chef Matt Wilde's foldable, puffy-edged 'Pilsen-style' pies — Old Style lager in the dough — born in Pilsen.
Quiet Pilsen café whose tres leches Rick Bayless has named his favourite.

F.ad: W Argyle St, Uptown (Asia on Argyle), Chicago
F.w: Argyle Street pho specialist — one of the city's best bowls, gently sweet and spiced.
Long-running Argyle Street Vietnamese dining room prized for consistency — shaking beef, tapioca dumplings, bún bò Huế.
Bridgeport Cantonese seafood house from the Wing Yip family — live-tank shellfish and wok-fried lobster over lap-cheong sticky rice.
Bridgeport's bargain Chinese tasting menu — four inventive courses for well under $40.
Counter-service Bridgeport grill stretching and baking Lebanese-style pita daily — shawarma and charred eggplant.
Chatham's healthy-leaning neighbourhood deli on the 75th Street 'Restaurant Row', named for owner Derrick Rowe's grandmother.

F.ad: W 47th St, Back of the Yards, Chicago, IL 60609
F.w: Back of the Yards Guerrero kitchen built on cecina — thin-pounded, marinated, grilled beef with guacamole and housemade tortillas.
